(Round 2's review found step 1 — `pulumi state delete` — refused in exactly the situation every consumer of the old releases is in; this round replaces it with two applies and `retainOnDelete: true`. proof.surface: A real `pulumi` v3.268.0 (the version the component's own module pins) on a local file backend, with the `command` provider v1.1.0, modelling the consumer's own shape: resource `service` stands in for the consumer's `tailscale.Service` and carries a `delete` command that appends to a marker file on disk, so a delete that really ran is visible; resource `consumer` takes `service`'s output into one of its inputs and names no `DependsOn`, which is how a stack that passed the Service's `Name` as `tailnetService` comes to depend on it. No credential and no network resource: the question is Pulumi's own behaviour.
proof.command: pulumi login file://<dir>/state; pulumi up --yes; pulumi state delete 'urn:pulumi:proof::proof::command:local:Command::service' --yes; then up with protect+retainOnDelete set and the resource removed from the program; then `pulumi state unprotect` and the same up; all at PULUMI_HOME on the issue volume
proof.observed: Three readings, all matching the README's new text. (1) `pulumi state delete` on the depended-on resource is refused: `error: urn:…::service can't be safely deleted because the following resources depend on it: * "consumer" (urn:…::consumer). Delete those resources first or pass --target-dependents.` The dependency came from an output flowing into an input alone, with no explicit DependsOn, which is exactly the consumer's case, so the README is right that `pulumi state delete` is not the route and right that the CLI's suggestion, `--target-dependents`, would take the dependents with it. (2) With `retainOnDelete: true` AND `protect` set, removing the resource is refused: `error: resource "urn:…::service" cannot be deleted because it is protected`, 2 errored, and the marker file stayed empty. So the README's instruction to unprotect in step 1 is necessary and not decoration: the retain does not get past protect. (3) Unprotected, with `retainOnDelete: true`, removing the resource gives `-  command:local:Command service deleted (0.00s)[retain]`, `- 1 deleted`, the state entry gone and THE MARKER FILE STILL EMPTY — the provider's delete never ran. That is the whole claim of the two-apply hand-over: the state entry goes and the live Service stays.
proof.negativeControl: The same removal without `retainOnDelete`: the resource was created again with the flag off, the program then dropped it, and the apply printed `-  command:local:Command service deleted (0.01s)` with no `[retain]` and the marker file read `DELETED-SERVICE`. So the provider's delete does run when the retain is absent, which is the hazard the README describes — removing the declaration without the retain deletes the Service the component has just adopted — and the retain is what stops it.
